title: Tariff Surcharge Credit-Memo Recovery for Mid-Size Manufacturers
one_liner: Mine a plant's accounts-payable history for 2025-26 tariff surcharges, then win credit memos from the distributors who are now receiving IEEPA refunds.
customer: US manufacturers with $5M-$200M revenue and 30-300 active vendors who paid line-item 'tariff surcharges' or tariff-justified price increases from March 2025 through the February 2026 Supreme Court ruling. The buyer is the CFO, controller or purchasing director.
problem: Refunds go to the importer of record, and importers of record are usually distributors: fastener houses, bearing and fitting suppliers, steel service centers, electronics distributors, tooling vendors. The plant paid the surcharge but has no claim with CBP. Downstream buyers have to rely on contract and unjust-enrichment theories against the vendor. Large retailers have law firms doing this, but a $4k-$60k claim per vendor is below any law firm's floor. Plant managers also will not sue the only source of a hydraulic fitting, so the claims are simply going unasked.
solution: 'SurchargeScan': connect to QuickBooks, NetSuite, Epicor or Infor (or upload AP PDFs). AI extracts surcharge lines and tariff-justified price-increase letters, ranks vendors by likelihood of being the importer of record (using public bill-of-lading data and vendor type), and generates reservation-of-rights letters. It then runs a relationship-preserving negotiation for credit memos against future orders instead of cash demands, and tracks each vendor's refund status through CBP's CAPE process. A partner law firm signs off on letters and escalates only large or hostile cases.
why_now: The Supreme Court held the IEEPA tariffs unlawful in February 2026. CBP launched its CAPE refund module on April 20, 2026, with well over $100B accepted for processing. The government is appealing the Court of International Trade's refund order, so vendors are receiving cash now while uncertainty still gives buyers leverage. Every month vendors book the windfall as profit, the claim gets harder to recover.
revenue_model: 20%-25% contingency on recovered credits and cash, plus a $499 scan fee credited against the fee. Average expected recovery of $25k-$150k per plant, with margins on a heavily automated flow. Later, an ongoing 'duty-pass-through audit' for any future tariff regime.
non_obvious_insight: Nobody in the surcharge fight wants to be in court with their own supplier. Plant managers will happily take a credit memo on the next PO but will never file a lawsuit, so the winning product is a diplomatic credit negotiation run by software, not a demand-letter factory.
first_30_days: Recruit 5 Ohio plant controllers as design partners with a free scan in return for 20% on recoveries. Build the scanner with an LLM over exported AP data plus a public bill-of-lading lookup. Send 20 reservation-of-rights letters and get the first credit memos booked. Sign a referral and review agreement with one trade-law boutique. Publish the recovery rate data from the first 10 vendors to sell the next 50 plants.

title: Mini Cat Bonds for Co-ops and Counties
one_liner: Cat bond capital is at record highs but deals under $50M are uneconomic. Make a $5-25M cat bond a 90-day, low-cost, template product for the sponsors the market ignores.
customer: Small public risk pools, rural electric cooperatives, counties, hospital systems and small regional insurers needing $5M-$50M of catastrophe protection.
problem: Cat bond issuance is a record $18.9B year to date with $65.6B outstanding, yet legal, modeling, rating and SPV costs of $1M-plus put small deals out of reach. Small sponsors stay in the traditional market or go bare, while primary property markets stay hard.
solution: A standardized private cat bond or collateralized reinsurance template: pre-approved documents, standard parametric triggers with an independent calculation agent, treasury-fund collateral with transparent accounting, and a target all-in cost under $150k with issuance in about 90 days. Sell the notes to ILS funds seeking diversification.
why_now: Record traditional and ILS capital, softening through 2027 (Jefferies), and mature tokenized and money-market collateral (Goldman put a $100B Treasury fund into crypto plumbing, CoinDesk 2026-09-28). ILS investors want diversification beyond Florida wind.
revenue_model: 1.5-3% of limit as a structuring fee, plus annual administration and calculation-agent fees.
non_obvious_insight: Softening means capital wants to deploy, so the binding constraint is deal cost per dollar of limit. That is a documentation and operations problem, not a risk-appetite problem.
first_30_days: Retain an offshore law firm and a calculation agent. Find two state pooling associations with wildfire or hail exposure, get indications of interest from two ILS funds, and produce a reusable term-sheet template. Charge a structuring retainer to fund first-deal work.

title: Licensed True Stories for Narration Channels
one_liner: A story studio that interviews real people about real events and licenses the recordings and scripts to faceless story-narration channels, replacing scraped Reddit posts and fake AI-written 'confessions'.
customer: Operators of faceless YouTube, TikTok and podcast channels that narrate AITA-style, revenge, workplace and relationship-drama stories, from solo operators to 10-person studios, plus audio-drama and story apps. They pay roughly $40-$150 per non-exclusive license.
problem: These channels' supply is scraped Reddit posts they don't own, since authors keep copyright and Reddit's data licenses go to AI firms, not YouTubers. YouTube's July 2025 'inauthentic content' rules specifically flag readings of material not created by the uploader and templated narrated stories, and in January 2026 YouTube terminated 16 channels with 35M combined subscribers. Mods keep banning reposts and fabricated or AI-written stories, so fresh, real material is drying up. Freelancers on Fiverr write fake 'Reddit stories' for $10-$30 that read as obvious slop.
solution: A 15-minute voice-interview app plus a human editor. The storyteller tells their story out loud, and the studio transcribes and structures it into a narration-ready script with a signed release, ID check and revenue share. Channels get a non-exclusive or exclusive license and a 'voice-verified first-person account' provenance certificate they can show as original-source proof. Authors earn a share of licensed views through tracked license codes. Storytellers are recruited off Reddit so mods aren't disrupted.
why_now: YouTube's inauthentic-content policy took effect on 15 July 2025 and was followed by the January 2026 termination wave, so channel operators now need defensible originality and provenance. At the same time AI-written fake stories have flooded the genre, and mods removing them has shrunk the pool of scrapeable real material.
revenue_model: $40-$150 per non-exclusive license, $300-$800 for exclusive first-run, and bundles such as $499 per month for 10 licenses. Authors get 40-50% of revenue. Later, sell format and option rights to audio-drama and TV producers.
non_obvious_insight: Buyers are not short of scripts but of defensible originality. People tell true stories brilliantly out loud and badly in writing, so the audio-interview format both raises quality and creates a provenance signal that a text LLM can't cheaply fake. Mods know the top-performing genres and that the people who post these stories mostly do it for validation, not money, so a paid $30 interview is an easy yes.
first_30_days: Recruit 30 storytellers through Facebook groups, Craigslist and small creator ads at $30 per story. Produce 60 scripts with Whisper transcription plus human editing. Sell a $199 pilot pack of 10 stories to 20 narration-channel operators, found through public channel emails and faceless-creator Discords. Ask for view data on the first videos to validate the revenue-share model, and use the results as the pitch for subscription bundles.

title: Permit Concierge for Rare-Plant and Reptile Sellers
angle: Pairing 1: Legal services, compliance & new regulations (EU AI Act, privacy, PFAS, right to repair, etc.) x Weird, niche and overlooked markets (hobbies, collectibles, faith communities, subcultures)
one_liner: A checkout-integrated paperwork and permit service that lets hobby breeders of orchids, aroids, cacti, tarantulas and reptiles legally fill foreign orders instead of pushing buyers to the gray market.
customer: Independent rare-plant sellers (Instagram, Etsy, Facebook groups), hobby reptile/amphibian/invertebrate breeders, and small orchid/succulent nurseries doing $3k+/month that keep turning away foreign orders. Expo organizers and hobby societies (aroid, orchid, reptile expos) are a channel.
problem: All orchids and cacti, plus many other hobby species, are CITES-listed. Cross-border shipments need phytosanitary certificates, CITES export/import permits (which vary by country and by whether specimens are artificially propagated), US Lacey Act declarations, and import-inspection compliance on the EU/UK side. CITES CoP20 (Nov-Dec 2025) added listings that phase in during 2026 (verify). The paperwork is per-shipment, per-country and slow, so honest sellers refuse foreign orders, buyers turn to smugglers, and a small mistake means seizure or fines.
solution: A per-shipment service. The seller enters species and origin (propagated or wild). The system determines required documents by destination (CITES appendix and exemptions, phytosanitary certificate, carrier acceptance rules), pre-fills forms, books inspections and generates paperwork packets. It maintains a 'propagation record book' for each seller (dated photos, invoices, mother-plant records) to evidence the artificially-propagated exemption. A Shopify/Etsy plug-in quotes or blocks foreign orders with the permit fee included. A licensed customs broker/permit expeditor is the operating partner, and a wildlife-law attorney handles edge cases.
why_now: New CITES listings from CoP20 phase in through 2026 (verify). Post-Brexit UK rules and the EU Plant Health Regulation (fully applicable since Dec 2019) mean plant parcels need phytosanitary certificates, and platform and law-enforcement attention to online wildlife trade keeps rising. Rare-plant and exotic-pet hobby demand stayed high after 2020, so more sellers are hitting the cliff.
revenue_model: $89-349 per shipment. $39/month pro plan that includes the propagation record book and checkout plug-in. Referral fees from carriers/brokers. Sponsored compliance desks at hobby expos.
non_obvious_insight: Enforcement targets traffickers, but the practical legal cliff is for honest small sellers. The exemption for artificially propagated specimens means documentation of propagation is the real product: a provenance book. A seller with a clean book can charge a premium and reach EU/UK buyers competitors cannot, and a 'permit-verified' badge becomes a moat as platforms tighten.
first_30_days: Pick one lane, either CITES-listed succulents/orchids US-to-EU/UK or captive-bred reptiles. Partner with an experienced permit expeditor. Publish a free 'what paperwork does my plant need' checker to collect leads. Sign 10 sellers with pending foreign orders and process 30 shipments at about $150 each. Use the results to build templates and the propagation-book format.

title: AI-Off Proficiency Checks for Clinicians
one_liner: E.M. Forster's The Machine Stops and Asimov's The Feeling of Power turned into recurrent, pilot-style checks that measure whether clinicians still perform well when the AI is switched off.
customer: GI and radiology group practices, hospital medical staff offices (ongoing professional practice evaluation and credentialing), physician-owned malpractice carriers seeking premium-credit evidence, and residency programs.
problem: Routine AI assistance may erode unaided skill. A 2025 Lancet Gastroenterology & Hepatology study of 19 experienced endoscopists in Poland found adenoma detection in non-AI colonoscopies fell from 28.4% to 22.4% after AI exposure (the study is observational and has been contested). No one measures unaided proficiency, unlike pilots' manual-flying currency, and outages or out-of-distribution cases will expose the gap.
solution: A quarterly, 25-minute, blinded and timed case set (videos and images with expert ground truth) delivered with AI overlays disabled. Scores are benchmarked against each clinician's own baseline and peer cohort, with drift alerts, targeted micro-drills, and a certificate for credentialing files and insurers. Add an AI-outage drill for departments (tabletop plus live). Start with colonoscopy, then extend to mammography and other AI-assisted reads.
why_now: AI computer-aided detection is now routine in colonoscopy and mammography. The deskilling study made the risk concrete and quotable. Malpractice carriers and hospital counsel are looking for defensible evidence, and the Joint Commission already requires ongoing professional practice evaluation.
revenue_model: $600-1,500 per clinician per year, carrier-funded programs paid per insured group, and enterprise licenses for health systems.
non_obvious_insight: Sell it as insurance evidence and credentialing paperwork, not education. Aviation shows regulators and insurers accept currency requirements once a failure mode is measured. The pre- and post-adoption unaided performance record is also what a hospital will need to defend an AI-related malpractice case, so buyers are motivated to start their baseline now.
first_30_days: License public polyp-video datasets and recruit two GI academic advisors to write ground truth. Build 10 case sets and pilot free for eight weeks with two GI groups. Pitch one physician-owned malpractice carrier on a premium credit for participating groups, then charge about $900 per clinician per year.

title: Robot Finger That Makes Legacy Instruments Agent-Operable
one_liner: A camera-plus-servo retrofit box that presses buttons, turns knobs and reads displays on validated lab and test equipment from the outside, giving decade-old instruments an API without touching their software.
customer: QC and analytical labs in pharma and CDMOs, food and environmental testing labs, university core facilities, and small biotechs running out-of-support equipment such as plate readers, autoclaves, centrifuges, HPLC pumps, stability chambers and test benches.
problem: Lab automation assumes new, API-enabled instruments, but the installed base is 10-20-year-old boxes with front panels only. In GxP and ISO 17025 labs, changing instrument firmware or software can trigger revalidation, which blocks IT-style integration. Scientists and agents still want unattended overnight runs, scheduling and structured logs.
solution: A clamp-on or adhesive module with 2-6 servos for buttons, knobs and a touchscreen stylus, a wide-angle camera, and a vision-language model that reads 7-segment displays, LCDs and status LEDs. A confirm-after-every-action loop and hard interlocks make it safe. It exposes an MCP and REST endpoint ('start program 4', 'read temperature', 'log state') and keeps video plus state log as the audit trail. It sits outside the validated boundary as 'operator-equivalent', so only the actuator needs qualification.
why_now: Vision-language models now read messy panels cheaply and reliably, and servo and edge-compute costs are trivial. Autonomous-lab offerings such as Ginkgo Cloud Lab prove scientists want agent-run experiments, but they require shipping samples to a vendor's lab. Most labs still own and must keep using their own equipment.
revenue_model: $400-900 hardware per instrument, $40-100 per month per device for scheduling, audit trail and the agent endpoint, and $2-5k per site for IQ/OQ qualification templates.
non_obvious_insight: Revalidation cost, not technology, blocks lab automation. An actuator that does exactly what a technician's finger does sidesteps change control, so selling 'validation-friendly' beats selling 'smart'. The video-verified state log is also a better audit trail than most instruments produce natively.
first_30_days: Build 3 prototypes from off-the-shelf servos, cameras and a Raspberry Pi-class board. Interview 20 QC lab managers and core-facility directors. Offer free two-week pilots on one autoclave or plate reader that runs a nightly routine, then convert to a $3k paid pilot including an IQ/OQ document.

title: Supply-House-Branded Back Office for Tiny Shops
one_liner: White-label quote, invoice, parts-pricing and trade-credit software delivered to solo-to-5-tech shops through their local independent supply house counter.
customer: Independent plumbing, HVAC, electrical and roofing supply houses and regional distributors squeezed by Home Depot (SRS, GMS, Mingledorff's) and Lowe's (FBM, Artisan). End users are their trade account holders.
problem: ServiceTitan fell about 26% after Q2 on slowing GTV, softer HVAC leads and a delay on exteriors, and expects only about 700 locations on its agentic tier. Most tiny shops have no operations layer and will not buy software cold, since CAC is brutal and churn high. Independent distributors are losing pro accounts to big-box integration and need a reason for contractors to stay.
solution: A private-label 'contractor OS' under the distributor's brand. Quotes are built from the distributor's live price book, invoices are text-to-pay, job notes and callbacks are tracked, truck stock reorders route to the counter, and net-30 parts credit is bundled. Counter staff onboard shops in person. It is free with a trade account, and the distributor pays per active shop.
why_now: Home Depot bought Mingledorff's in May 2026 on top of SRS and GMS, and Lowe's bought FBM for $8.8B. Independents' backs are against the wall. ServiceTitan's drop and deprioritization of exteriors leave small shops ignored. LLM-assisted development makes a lightweight tool cheap to build.
revenue_model: $30-60 per active shop per month paid by the distributor, or 0.25-0.5% of the shop's parts spend. Add payments interchange share and parts-financing spread.
non_obvious_insight: Vertical software wins on distribution. The supply house counter is the one place every tiny shop shows up every week, and distributors have both a strategic reason (defense against big-box) and a budget to pay for stickiness. Contractors will adopt anything that makes parts pricing and credit easier.
first_30_days: Sign two independent supply houses through buying-group contacts. Build an MVP on price-book CSV upload, SMS quotes and Stripe. Pilot with 20 shops per distributor and measure parts spend lift per shop.

title: Apprentice Athlete: Injury-Proofing the Skilled Trades
one_liner: An 8-week pre-apprenticeship that conditions and movement-screens new electricians, plumbers and pipefitters so they survive the first two years.
customer: Joint apprenticeship training centers (IBEW/NECA, UA, IEC, ABC), community-college trade programs, and the workers' comp carriers and brokers behind contractors. Contractors pay per placed apprentice.
problem: Electricians have about 72.7k openings a year (data-center demand) and plumbers about 42k, but the 4-5 year apprenticeship path is bottlenecked by employer sponsors and weak pre-apprenticeship screening. Overexertion and strain injuries are consistently a leading cause of lost-time injuries and feed early attrition. Many entrants are sedentary career-changers, including displaced white-collar grads (42% of recent grads are underemployed).
solution: 'Apprentice Athlete' runs 3 sessions a week for 8 weeks in existing gyms, taught by athletic trainers and strength coaches. It uses trade-specific drills (overhead conduit work, ladder and pipe carries, crawlspace mobility, grip endurance), phone-video or cheap-wearable movement screens, and an injury-prevention curriculum. Completion, not a fitness score, earns JATC pre-apprenticeship credit and can slot in as a short program eligible for Workforce Pell where approved. It is structured as training rather than a hiring screen, to stay clear of ADA limits.
why_now: Workforce Pell launched July 1, 2026 but only 5 programs are approved. Apprenticeship-linked programs get a fast lane, and up to 49% of instruction can be delivered by employers or unions. Data-center demand is pulling electricians, and AI-exposed grads are pivoting to trades. Phone pose-estimation and cheap wearables are now good enough to measure movement quality.
revenue_model: $400-800 per apprentice per cohort paid by contractor, JATC or Pell/WIOA funds. A $100-200k pilot contract with a comp carrier tied to premium credits. Then per-seat licensing to gyms and trainers who run the program (they keep 60-70%).
non_obvious_insight: The trades treat the body as a consumable, while sports treat it as an appreciating asset. Comp carriers already have loss runs showing injuries cluster in the first 24 months, so a $600 conditioning program pays back if it prevents one strain claim per few dozen apprentices. Trade schools cannot have that ROI conversation, but insurers can.
first_30_days: Partner with one IEC/ABC chapter or a community-college trades program. Run a 6-week pilot for 20 career-changers using phone-video screening and a $50 tracker. Log attendance, attrition and minor injuries against the prior cohort. Take the numbers to the contractors' workers' comp broker to negotiate a premium-credit pilot.

title: Junior Studio OS for Teen Game Developers
one_liner: Payroll, enforceable contracts, a custodial legal shell and payout splitting for teenage Roblox and Fortnite creator teams that already run large studios without knowing they are businesses.
customer: Teen (13-19) founders of UGC game studios and their parents, plus adult publishers, investors and acquirers who want to back teen studios safely.
problem: Roblox creators earned over $1.5B in 2025, and top studios are run by teens and early twenties. But minors can disaffirm contracts, collaborators across countries expect revenue splits, payouts land in personal or parent accounts, taxes are misunderstood, and there is no cap table. Disputes and co-founders who leave with the IP kill studios, and investors avoid them.
solution: A 'studio in a box': a custodial LLC or UTMA structure with guardian co-signature and court-approval flow for larger deals. A rev-share ledger reads DevEx and group payouts and splits them automatically. It collects W-9/W-8 forms and sets aside tax reserves. It provides a parent-co-signed, ratify-at-18 contract template with IP assignment and vesting, plus a diligence data room for acquirers.
why_now: Roblox creator payouts were over $1.5B in 2025 (about 70% year-over-year growth), the standard DevEx rate rose to $0.0038 per Robux in September 2025, and 2026 rate changes reward higher-spending audiences. Teen studios are hiring peers and getting publisher attention. Fortnite (UEFN) and Minecraft marketplaces add more teen earners.
revenue_model: SaaS of $19-$49 per month per studio plus 1-2% on managed payouts, a $500-$2,500 legal setup package, and diligence or introduction fees from publishers and investors.
non_obvious_insight: Their barrier is not creativity, it is legal personhood. When a 15-year-old's game earns $20k per month, the biggest risk is a co-founder who quits with the IP or a signature that is not binding. Selling enforceable trust wins the studio and later the deal flow, making the OS the accepted source of diligence on teen studios.
first_30_days: Join the top 50 Roblox developer Discords and the DevForum. Offer a free 'who owns what' studio audit to 30 teen studios. Sell a $299 done-for-you custodial entity plus rev-share agreement drafted by a youth-entertainment lawyer, and get 10 paying by day 30. Pitch three UGC publishers on sourcing through you.

title: Open-Banking Rails for EU Connected Products
one_liner: A consent-and-access hub that lets manufacturers meet the EU Data Act's access-by-design duty and lets owners route product data to repairers, insurers and energy optimizers through one integration.
customer: Two sides. Forced buyers are manufacturers, importers and white-labelers of connected products sold in the EU (e-bikes, heat pumps, wallboxes, appliances, machinery, agricultural kit, wearables), paying per product family per year. The network side is independent repair chains, insurers, energy retailers, lenders and fleet managers paying per authorized device pull.
problem: Since 12 Sept 2026, connected products newly placed on the EU market must give users free, structured, machine-readable access to their data and share it with third parties on request. Most SME makers and importers have cloud endpoints never designed for this: no consent flow, no standard API, no logging, no trade-secret safeguards, no pre-sale disclosures. Third parties who want the data face hundreds of separate negotiations.
solution: A hosted 'Data Act portal' for the manufacturer covering ownership binding (QR or serial on the product), machine-readable export, consent to share with a named third party, trade-secret safeguards, access logs, a dispute workflow and the Art. 3(2) pre-contract disclosure templates. A normalized schema catalog per product category (for example 'heat pump v1') means third parties integrate once. We sell it first as a 90-day compliance kit, then monetize the network.
why_now: The access-by-design duty took effect 12 Sept 2026 and law-firm alerts show many makers unfinished. From 12 Jan 2027 cloud switching fees vanish, which makes data mobility a political priority. The regulation mandates giving data but says nothing about how anyone receives it.
revenue_model: Compliance SaaS at roughly EUR 300-3,000/month per product family. Network fees of EUR 0.02-0.50 per device per month from third-party consumers of the data. An optional certification badge for makers.
non_obvious_insight: The Data Act is open banking for machines, but with no PSD2-style standardization mandate: it creates a duty to give data with no way to receive it. Whoever standardizes the receiving side becomes the Plaid of physical products. The manufacturers, who are forced buyers today, pay for the network build.
first_30_days: Pick one fragmented vertical (e-bikes, or heat pumps and wallboxes). Publish a free 'is my product in scope' checker and a readiness checklist to generate leads. Sign 5 SME makers or importers to EUR 2k pilots that deliver a working access endpoint. Pitch two independent repair, insurance or energy firms as first consumers on the receiving side.

title: Pre-Cut Electrical Kits Per House Plan
one_liner: A regional kitting shop ships each production home's wiring as pre-cut, labeled, bundled kits so a helper pulls and a journeyman only terminates and inspects.
customer: Electrical subcontractors serving production and spec builders (5-100 homes a year), and builders in data-center-hot markets such as Texas.
problem: Data centers absorb electricians (nearly a third of the shortage; journeymen on overtime gross $130-170K, vendor stat), and Texas builders report electrical delays of up to 2 months. Meanwhile much rough-in time goes to measuring, cutting and pulling, which does not need a licensed person's minutes.
solution: For each repeat plan, generate a wire schedule and build kits: cable pre-cut and labeled by room and circuit, boxes pre-assembled, home runs pre-bundled, panel schedule pre-printed, delivered in numbered bins by phase. Lower-skill pullers or apprentices do most of the rough-in under supervision, and the journeyman terminates and inspects.
why_now: Electrician arbitrage from data-center overtime, builders with idle houses waiting on electrical, and digital plan libraries that expose structured circuit data. Wire-processing machines are cheap and used equipment is plentiful.
revenue_model: Materials plus 15-25%, or $2-4K per home, with a share of labor savings. Licensing the process to kitting shops in other metros.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce resource is journeyman minutes on tasks a journeyman does not need to do. Commercial contractors have prefabbed for decades, but residential never did because labor was cheap, and now the ROI is large.
first_30_days: Pick one production builder's most repeated plan. Hire an ex-electrician estimator and buy or rent a used cut-and-label machine. Sell kits for five homes to the builder's electrical sub and measure hours saved per house.

title: Live Doom-Pile Sessions for Avoided Paperwork
one_liner: A scheduled video session where a calm, admin-savvy host sits with you while you open the unopened mail pile, triages it, and gets the scary items handled before you hang up.
customer: Adults 25-55 with ADHD, anxiety, depression, recent bereavement or new-parent overload pay $59 per session or $89 a month for two sessions. Employer benefit programs, credit unions and probate attorneys pay for seats.
problem: Millions of people leave envelopes and portal notifications unopened because not knowing is more comfortable than knowing. Late fees, collections, missed renewals and tax notices escalate. The avoidance is emotional, so productivity apps and reminder tools do not touch it.
solution: A 45-minute weekly 'Admin Sunday' session. Members upload photos of the pile beforehand and AI produces a triage card (ignore, do this month, act by Friday). A trained host, such as a former paralegal, bookkeeper or benefits caseworker, sits with the member on camera as each envelope is opened. Three actions get done in the session, such as calling with a script, setting up a payment plan, or filing a form. The member leaves with a 'Nothing Scary' summary. A mail-forwarding tier serves people who cannot face even the session.
why_now: Adult ADHD diagnoses have surged and body-doubling is mainstream on TikTok and in tools like Focusmate. LLMs make triage and drafting nearly free, so one human can run 6-8 sessions a day and the business keeps a healthy margin. Collections on federal student loans restarted in 2025, raising the stakes of ignored mail. Consumers now value human presence precisely because AI can read the letter but cannot sit next to you.
revenue_model: $89 monthly subscription for two sessions, $59 a la carte. Hosts are paid $28-35 an hour, giving roughly 55-60% gross margin. B2B seats at $12-20 per employee per month for EAP and financial-wellness buyers.
non_obvious_insight: The product is courage with a witness, not productivity. People will pay to discover bad news in the company of someone calm. Silent co-working apps do not solve this because the body double is not allowed to help, and AI alone cannot absorb the emotion of opening the envelope.
first_30_days: Post in ADHD and adulting communities and make short 'doom pile' videos. Run 10 free consented live sessions to create content and testimonials. Sell $49 founding-member sessions through Stripe and run on Zoom and Google Drive. Recruit 5 hosts from retired paralegal and bookkeeper groups. Goal: 15 paying subscribers by day 30 and 30 by day 60.

title: Alcohol Bridge: GLP-1 Addiction Care for Hospitals
one_liner: A hospital-embedded service that starts naltrexone plus semaglutide at discharge for alcohol use disorder with PEth monitoring.
customer: Hospital addiction-consult teams and liver clinics, plus health plans and employers paying for alcohol-related admissions.
problem: Only ~2% of people with alcohol use disorder get medication. A Lancet RCT (May 2026, n=108) showed semaglutide cut heavy drinking days in AUD with obesity, with NNT ~4.3 vs 7+ for approved drugs, and NIH-reported work shows added benefit on top of CBT. Phase 3 trials and the VA's CRAVE trial are running, but clinicians have no protocol, and opioid bridge clinics got settlement money while alcohol, the bigger killer, got none.
solution: A bridge service at discharge: naltrexone alone or with semaglutide (per trial eligibility, BMI 30 or more), PEth blood monitoring every 4 weeks, telehealth follow-ups and a cash-pay pill pathway, with outcome reporting on readmissions and PEth negatives.
why_now: The first RCT and NIH coverage landed in 2026, GLP-1s are now cheap and familiar, and hospitals are under margin pressure from readmissions. Off-label use requires careful protocols, so first movers will set the standard.
revenue_model: $250-400 per patient per month billed to hospitals, payers or employers, plus grant and state SUD funds where eligible.
non_obvious_insight: Alcohol-related admissions repeat and cost the hospital, but no service line owns the medication step. The wedge is a discharge protocol, not a new clinic.
first_30_days: Approach 3 hospital addiction-consult teams and hepatology clinics. Recruit an addiction-boarded medical director and run a 30-patient quality-improvement pilot under the hospital's existing governance, charging a ~$20k pilot fee.

title: Release-Date Congestion Map and Collision Cover
one_liner: A wishlist-overlap model and anonymous date-slot registry that tells indies where launch windows are crowded, later backed by parametric cover if a mega-title lands on top of them.
customer: Self-publishing indie developers and small publishers with 20k+ wishlists, and later insurers and MGAs underwriting launch risk.
problem: GTA VI launches 2026-11-19, and other publishers are rescheduling around it. Silksong (about 5.2M wishlists, 7M+ sales by Dec 2025) pushed several indies to delay after its date was announced. Devs lock marketing spend, then a giant date shifts. When everyone dodges the same date, they pile into the same safe windows, creating new collisions.
solution: Ingest public Steam wishlist ranks, release calendars and creator schedules to produce a congestion map and a per-title collision score based on audience overlap. Add a confidential slot registry where publishers submit intended dates and get congestion feedback. Once loss data exists, add parametric cover paying out if a listed mega-title moves within +/-14 days of a locked date.
why_now: GTA VI is the largest release-calendar shock in years and its ripple lasts months. Q1 2027 herd behavior is forming now, and no one measures collision risk.
revenue_model: $49-299 per month SaaS or $500 per date report, plus a 15-25% MGA commission on parametric premiums (3-6% of cover).
non_obvious_insight: Collision is treated as luck, but it is measurable through audience overlap and tradeable as a parametric risk. The herd effect, everyone avoiding the same date, is a coordination failure a neutral registry can fix.
first_30_days: Scrape Steam release calendars and wishlist ranks. Publish a free Q1 2027 congestion map on Discord and Reddit dev communities. Sell 20 paid date reports and speak to 3 MGAs about a pilot cover.

title: Inherited Low-Rate Mortgage Concierge for Heirs
angle: Pairing 2: Real estate x death/estates/wealth transfer
one_liner: A flat-fee service that helps heirs keep, assume or transfer a parent's low-rate mortgage instead of paying it off at closing, and values that rate as an estate asset so siblings can buy each other out fairly.
customer: Heirs (Gen X, aged 45-60) who inherit a home with a mortgage at 3-4% while new loans cost about 7.5%. The estate attorneys, probate realtors and bank trust officers who advise them refer clients and pay for tooling.
problem: The default estate path is to sell the house and pay off the loan, which destroys below-market financing. On a $300K balance at about 3.25% with 22 years left versus 7.5%, the rate is worth roughly $90K in present value (my calculation). Federal rules generally bar lenders from calling loans due on transfer to relatives at death, and confirmed successors have servicing rights under CFPB rules, but servicers are slow and inconsistent and heirs do not know. Siblings often cannot buy each other out at current rates, and a buyer's market with concessions on 44.7% of sales makes forced sales costlier.
solution: Within days of a death, verify loan type, rate, balance and assumability and confirm successor-in-interest status with the servicer. Bridge payments during probate, and produce a Rate Asset Report that values the rate for the estate inventory so heirs can split fairly. Structure buyouts with junior notes or partner lenders so one heir keeps or rents the house, and for sellers show where FHA or VA assumability lifts the sale price. Confirm applicability with counsel, since protections generally cover owner-occupied 1-4 unit homes.
why_now: Rates are rising again (Redfin: futures price the Fed funds rate at 5% by end-2027, and the 30-year is about 7.4-7.6%). A large share of Boomer mortgages sit below 4%, and the first wave of the transfer is arriving. Record concessions make selling into this market expensive. ROAD to Housing Act limits on institutional single-family owners push heirs to be small landlords.
revenue_model: $1,500-2,500 flat fee per estate or a share of rate-value preserved, a $499 Rate Asset Report, referral fees from buyout lenders, and $200 per month tooling subscriptions for probate attorneys.
non_obvious_insight: The great wealth transfer is counted in balance-sheet dollars, but in a 7.5% world the most valuable asset in many middle-class estates is the interest rate on the parent's mortgage, and the default estate process throws it away at closing.
first_30_days: Write servicer letter templates and an assumability checklist reviewed by an attorney. Recruit five probate attorneys and three probate realtors. Launch the $499 Rate Asset Report to estates with mortgages and track how many convert to the full service. Sign one HELOC or non-QM lender as buyout-financing partner.

title: Cross-Lender Double-Pledge Registry for Receivables
one_liner: A hashed, shared ledger where lenders confirm that an invoice, receivable or auto loan has not already been pledged elsewhere, starting with freight and trade factoring.
customer: Independent factoring companies, ABL desks at regional banks, supply-chain-finance funds and private-credit lenders to mid-market suppliers.
problem: First Brands allegedly double- and triple-pledged about $2.3B of invoices. The SEC charged Tricolor's former CEO and CFO on 18 Aug 2026 with double-pledging subprime auto loans to multiple lenders and securitisations. No single funder can detect overlap because there is no mechanism for lenders to see each other's pledges, so small factors are hit constantly.
solution: Members submit hashed invoice fingerprints (debtor ID, invoice number, amount, date) by API and get 'clean' or 'conflict' back in seconds. Add automated debtor confirmation (email, portal and EDI checks that the invoice exists and where payment is directed) and remittance-diversion alerts. Use private set intersection or salted hashes so lenders never reveal borrowers, and a consortium contract plus UCC-style notice.
why_now: First Brands and Tricolor collapsed in Sept 2025, and DOJ (Jan 2026) and SEC (Aug 2026) actions followed. Private credit's growth, investor demands for collateral verification and bar-association guidance on being 'two-timed' have created board-level urgency.
revenue_model: $0.10-2 per query, $1-5k per month membership for small factors, $50k+ per year for funds, and $5-15 per automated debtor confirmation.
non_obvious_insight: Fraud lives in the gaps between lenders, not inside them. The data everyone needs (each other's pledges) is data nobody will share bilaterally. A neutral registry sells a network effect for detection, like Carfax or the UK's Cifas, rather than a better anomaly detector.
first_30_days: Start with freight factoring, where duplicate invoices and fake brokers are a known problem. Sign 10 independent factors and two fintech ABL lenders through industry associations, build the hashing API, and offer founding members a free tier in exchange for contributing data.

title: Wildfire Evacuation Autopilot for Campsites and Hotels
one_liner: Satellite fire-spread alerts plus pre-contracted buses, routes and multilingual guest messaging turn every tourist lodging in fire country into an evacuation node.
customer: Campsites, holiday parks and hotels in fire-prone Mediterranean regions (France's Aude, Var and Gironde, Catalonia, Greece, Portugal, Croatia), plus regional tourism boards and insurers.
problem: Summer wildfires now force sudden evacuations of thousands of tourists who have no local knowledge, often no cars and no shared language. Duty of care sits with small operators holding paper plans they have never drilled, while insurers tighten terms.
solution: A site-specific evacuation plan with two routes and a refuge, ingestion of hourly fire detections (NASA FIRMS, Copernicus EFFIS and commercial satellite feeds), wind-aware fire arrival estimates per site, and automatic guest alerts by WhatsApp or SMS in the guest's language using check-in data. It includes a staff checklist and drills, and standby contracts with local coach operators.
why_now: Higher-frequency satellite fire detection arrived with early-2025 launches such as FireSat, and wildfire seasons in 2025 were severe across Southern Europe. Insurers and regulators are pressing small operators.
revenue_model: EUR 300-1,200 per site per year, margin on coach standby retainers, insurer premium-discount share and regional government contracts.
non_obvious_insight: Tourist lodging is the largest concentration of people in fire zones with no local knowledge, no vehicles and no common language, and the legal duty sits with operators who cannot afford risk consultants.
first_30_days: Recruit 25 campsites in Aude, Hérault, Var and Gironde through the camping federation. Deliver a plan PDF and WhatsApp alerts at EUR 390 per year, run one drill and pitch two insurers with results.

title: Yes-in-God's-Backyard Deal Desk for Congregations
angle: Pairing 1: Legal services, compliance & new regulations (EU AI Act, privacy, PFAS, right to repair, etc.) x Weird, niche and overlooked markets (hobbies, collectibles, faith communities, subcultures)
one_liner: A fixed-fee service that tells a shrinking congregation and its denomination what its land can legally become (by-right housing, ground lease, sale, merger), then runs the governance, title and buyer process.
customer: Regional denominational bodies (presbyteries, dioceses, Methodist conferences, Lutheran synods, synagogue federations) and boards of congregations with 50-250 members that hold a large building and lot they cannot afford to maintain. Secondary payers are affordable-housing developers and community land trusts that need sites.
problem: Per the briefing, only 33% of Americans attend monthly, Christian share has plateaued near 62%, and 18-24-year-olds are only 46% Christian, so many congregations sit on oversized buildings whose upkeep drains endowments. Selling is legally tangled: denominational trust clauses and canon-law approval thresholds, donor-restricted funds and cemeteries, state attorney-general notice for charitable assets, historic designation, and zoning. Lay boards typically wait for a crisis and then accept the first offer, usually an investor or another church. Meanwhile housing-shortage politics have produced by-right housing on religious land laws (California SB 4 took effect in 2024, with similar bills in other states, verify list), so the land may be worth multiples of the building, but few boards know it.
solution: Lead with a $1,500-3,000 'Land Options Report' covering parcel and zoning analysis under the state's faith-land housing law, likely unit yield, estimated residual land value against as-is sale, a title and restriction checklist, and a governance map of who must approve (trust clause, canon law, AG notice). Then sell a fixed-fee 'Transition Package': sequenced legal steps, member-vote scripts and communications, an RFP to pre-qualified faith-friendly developers (ground lease with a worship-space carve-out, so the congregation keeps a chapel and gets rent), and closing management. The report is automated with county parcel data plus LLM extraction of zoning code, reviewed by a real-estate/nonprofit attorney.
why_now: Pew's 2025 finding that decline has leveled but the generational gap is steep (briefing) means closures will keep coming for years. By-right faith-land housing laws are new (California SB 4 effective 2024, more states 2025-26, verify) and few boards know they exist. Cheap parcel data and LLM zoning-code reading make a $1,500 report profitable, where it used to need a $15k consultant.
revenue_model: Report fee of $1.5-3k, paid by congregations or as a bulk judicatory contract of $25-60k per year. Transition package at a fixed $15-40k or 1.5-3% of transaction value. Developer-side site-sourcing retainer or finder's fee, structured around broker-licensing rules.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce resource is not money or developers but a governance process a lay board can survive: each closure has 4-6 approval gates and any one can veto it. The value sits in a pre-mapped approval path for each denomination's polity. Under by-right housing, the residual land value often exceeds the building's as-is price, so the congregation that thinks it must close can instead become a landlord with a rent-paying chapel. Church brokers and developers each see only half of this.
first_30_days: Choose one state with a faith-land housing law and one denomination whose polity is well documented. Offer free Land Options Reports to 10 congregations referred by a regional official, in exchange for case-study rights and a $500 deposit. Hire a part-time real-estate/nonprofit attorney, assemble county GIS and zoning data, and pre-qualify 3 developers. Aim for 3-5 paid reports and one transition engagement within six months.

title: Recall-Proofing Subscription for Small Pet Food Brands
one_liner: Outsourced food-safety plans, pooled H5N1/Salmonella/Listeria testing and label review for the hundreds of small raw, freeze-dried and topper brands that cannot afford a QA department.
customer: Small raw, freeze-dried, topper and mixer brands and their co-packers, including Shopify-native brands.
problem: FDA now requires makers of cat and dog food using uncooked or unpasteurized poultry, dairy or egg ingredients to reanalyze their food safety plans for H5N1 under the animal-food preventive controls rule, after cats died from contaminated raw food. A recall can kill a small brand, and the fast-growing topper and mixer category (purchases +214% since 2018 per the briefing) creates label and 'complete and balanced' compliance ambiguity.
solution: A monthly subscription with PCQI-qualified plan writing and upkeep, supplier verification, a pooled testing program at negotiated lab prices with a certificate-of-analysis dashboard, mock-recall drills and label review against current AAFCO and state rules. Bundle with a recall-insurance partner for lower premiums.
why_now: FDA's H5N1 reanalysis requirement (announced January 2025) turned a news event into a permanent compliance line item. DTC consolidation (Farmer's Dog's first acquisition) raises supplier-diligence standards for small brands seeking exits.
revenue_model: $500-2,000 per month subscription, 20-30% margin on pooled testing pass-through, and insurance referral fees.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders treat H5N1 as an outbreak headline. For small brands it is a permanent, recurring cost, and testing volume can be pooled across many brands to get lab prices and QA depth no single brand can afford, the same economics that supports outsourced food-safety consultants in human food.
first_30_days: List 300 raw and freeze-dried brands from FDA registration and social listings. Send a free H5N1 gap audit against FDA's reanalysis requirement. Contract a PCQI consultant and one accredited lab. Convert 5-10 brands to paid subscriptions.

title: Escrow and Tax Rails for Agent-Hired Humans
one_liner: The compliance and payment layer that lets software agents legally hire humans for judgment and real-world tasks: owner KYC, task-legality screening, escrow, worker classification and tax forms.
customer: Agent-framework developers and companies whose agents need on-call humans (verification, phone calls, notarisation, in-person checks), plus the workers doing the tasks. Take rate is 8-12%.
problem: Agent-to-human marketplaces are appearing (47jobs, Hirenewtalent.ai in the brief, and viral 'rent a human' sites in early 2026), but nobody is the clear payor, employer or liable party. Who issues 1099s, who is responsible if an agent sends someone to do something illegal or never pays, and how do workers avoid scams?
solution: An API plus MCP tool ('ask_human'): agents post tasks against funded escrow tied to a KYC'd human or company principal. A legality and safety classifier rejects risky tasks. Automatic tax forms and classification, dispute arbitration and two-sided reputation follow, with optional injury insurance for physical tasks.
why_now: Agent frameworks and MCP matured in 2025, agent-payment standards and stablecoin rails are being rolled out, and agent-run marketplaces are going viral. Regulators will demand a principal of record after the first scandal.
revenue_model: 8-12% take rate on tasks plus an insurance margin for physical work.
non_obvious_insight: The marketplace is cheap to clone. The moat is the principal-of-record and liability layer, which is what regulators and enterprise buyers will eventually require, so building the compliant rails first wins the boring middle.
first_30_days: Ship a minimal escrow API and MCP tool with 200 vetted workers in one niche (phone verification calls, document notarisation, local checks in 3 cities). Onboard 10 agent builders through Discord and HN and complete the first 500 paid tasks.
